# Vex

> Vex is a TypeScript library for typed spreadsheet formulas over domain objects. A Vex program evaluates at one key of a space of records. It reads fields relative to that key, combines them with the ops of domains (for example 2D vectors), and gives a value or an error value with a code like #REF! or #N/A. Axes evaluate a body at related keys (all, others, other, neighbors, where), and reductions combine the results. A program is plain JSON data.

To write a Vex program as data, follow the JSON Schema of the IR: https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/ir.schema.json. Then check the program with `parse(text, domains)` of `@mark1russell7/vex`, and evaluate it with `evaluate(expr, { space, origin, domains })`. A program can also be a document of coeval, for example `{ "type": ["ops", "add"], "value": [{ "type": "ref", "value": ["self", "n"] }, 1] }`: refer to https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/reference/ir/#documents. The kernel of coeval checks a document by the contracts of `VEX_WORLD`, and `kernelPlan` evaluates it in the kernel, as the reference tier. `agree` of a plan compares the tiers of the kernel with a tier that you give. `explain` gives a trace of each node, with the reads of each reference. A program does not throw: each failure is an error value with a code, a kind, a message, the path of its node, the origin and the focus.

## Docs

- [Tour](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/learn/tour/): the builder, one call at a time
- [Concepts](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/learn/concepts/): space, origin, focus, address, axis, domain, result
- [Axes](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/learn/axes/): the relations between positions, and the reductions
- [Sheets and cycles](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/learn/sheets/): named columns that read each other, and #CYCLE!
- [Vectors](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/learn/vectors/): one value for the math of two dimensions, and how to make, reduce and read vectors
- [Error values](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/learn/errors/): the codes, and how errors go up the tree
- [The IR](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/reference/ir/): the kinds of expression, the moves, the axes
- [The API](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/reference/api/): the functions and the types of the packages
- [The specification](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/spec/): each rule with its requirement ID and its test status

## For agents

- [The skill of Vex](https://github.com/mark1russell7/vex/blob/main/plugins/vex/skills/vex/SKILL.md): the model, the rules, a first program, the IR, and when to make a domain or report a gap
- [The catalog of the domains](https://github.com/mark1russell7/vex/blob/main/plugins/vex/skills/vex/reference/catalog.md): each domain and each op, with its call, its result and its laws. A test makes it from the code.
- [Recipes](https://github.com/mark1russell7/vex/blob/main/plugins/vex/skills/vex/reference/recipes.md): a total over a tree, a running position, a lookup, loops, the compiler and programs as data
- [Make a domain](https://github.com/mark1russell7/vex/blob/main/plugins/vex/skills/vex/reference/domains.md): an example, the checklist, and the rules for a standalone module
- [Versions](https://github.com/mark1russell7/vex/blob/main/plugins/vex/skills/vex/reference/versions.md): the features of each version. Find the installed version before you use a feature.

## Optional

- [The Lab](https://mark1russell7.github.io/vex/lab/): edit a program as JSON and evaluate it
- [The source](https://github.com/mark1russell7/vex)
